Why do we need to sleep.

Considering humans are a social species, sleeping in a group mitigates a lot of risk as well as living in protected environments such as caves and trees. Looking at other animal kingdoms such as fish, we observe that their "sleep" cycles are much different, with some species only resting one part of the brain at a time. As far as the necessity for sleep, our big brains produce waste products through out the day which require a period of rest activity to be removed. As far as the origin of sleep, there's not a definitive consensus as of yet, though it appears that there is an evolutionary advantage for a species to be more active during parts of the day in exchange for reduced periods of activity in other parts.

I really enjoyed the Stuff You Should Know podcast on sleep, it covers a lot of these questions: http://www.stuffyoushouldknow.com/podcasts/is-sleep-that-important/

The short answer is that we really don't know, but we have some guesses.

 

Here's some websites to help you on your research: http://healthysleep.med.harvard.edu/healthy/matters/benefits-of-sleep/why-do-we-sleep

http://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-32606341
It's one of the big open question left in biology. It's quite astonishing we don't know exactly why we do something we spend 1/3 of our lives doing.
Aside from what others have said (which is spot on), there are animals that only sleep one hemisphere of their brain at a time, for the exact reason you mentioned.
Sleep economizes energy and consumption of resources. It might be better to ask why do we wake. The answer to that is not so mysterious. We wake to eat and procreate.
